observations: The original availability experiment failed: only 66 eligible pedestrian sources. The authorized outcome-blind amendment produced 26 fresh sources, with pedestrian 1 FIT/1 TEST. Original failed-run knowledge is byte-unchanged.

Both FIT rules selected hybrid1 for electricity. TEST mean MSE improved for both models; TimesFM hybrid1 remained worse than seasonal-naive24, while Bolt hybrid1 was slightly better than seasonal-naive24. This is a small exploratory pilot, not confirmed generalization.

M4 FIT-selected policies worsened TEST MSE for both models: Bolt past_selector3 slightly, TimesFM hybrid3 substantially. All fixed TimesFM M4 hindcast selectors had small positive TEST gains, but no best TEST selector depth is deployed.

Traffic hindcast selectors selected native on all four TEST sources for both models and all depths, avoiding harm on all three sources with main extraction. The fourth source abstained from extraction.

Electricity hindcasts missed opportunities: TimesFM depth1/2 accepted only one of three beneficial extracted hybrids; depth3 rejected all three. Bolt selectors accepted harmful electricity hybrids. Thus retrospective selector success does not transfer uniformly across domains.
Pedestrian n=1 TEST: all hybrids harmed both models; the frozen selectors and FIT policy retained native. Descriptive only, no CI or significance claim.
Fitted-tone-plus-last-residual at depth3 had worse TEST mean MSE than native in every model/domain cell. Full output-free and depth curves remain in analysis; no TEST-selected depth was promoted.
Frequency/amplitude stability and extraction abstention across origins are preserved per source as descriptive potential cues; no threshold was learned from TEST.
